items.title: Rising Domestic Violence Cases Push Peel Shelters Past Capacity
items.summary: Local leaders say Peel Region's provincially funded emergency shelters are stretched thin as intimate partner violence cases climb, with outdated funding rules making it harder to keep up. Mississauga's mayor and Peel Regional Council are now pressing the province for additional support.

First West Nile Case of the Season Turns Up in Peel Mosquitoes
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, this year's first local case of West Nile virus has turned up in mosquitoes near Queen Street East and Kennedy Road North in Brampton. The City says most infections are just mild, flu-like symptoms, though it can rarely affect the brain or nervous system, and it's urging Peel residents to start taking precautions against mosquito bites.

items.title: City Opens New Round of Public Engagement Sessions This August
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is inviting residents and businesses to weigh in on upcoming plans, programs and services through information sessions, open houses, workshops and online surveys throughout August. City staff say the feedback helps shape where time and resources get focused next.

items.title: Mississauga Voters Urged to Check the Voters' List Before October Election
items.summary: Mississauga heads to the polls on Monday, October 26 to elect its Mayor, Ward and Regional Councillors, and School Board Trustees for the 2026 to 2030 term. The City is encouraging residents to confirm or update their information on the Voter Registration Portal ahead of time, since being on the voters' list speeds up the process on election day.
